LESSON: METALS AND ALLOYS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIREMENT
Strand: Mixtures, Elements and Compounds
Topic 1.2: Metals and Alloys
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 16

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Metals and Alloys, part of Mixtures, Elements and Compounds in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 INTEGRATED SCIENCE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIREMENT.

Key inquiry question: How are alloys important in day-to-day life? 2. How does understanding rusting contribute to the preservation and maintenance of metal objects?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Metals and Alloys together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: The learner develops teamwork skills while working with peers to discuss the

composition of common alloys.

● Digital literacy: The learner develops the skill of interacting with technology as they manipulate digital devices while

searching for information on the physical and chemical properties of metals and common alloys.

Values:
● Respect: Learner accommodates others’ opinions during group discussions on uses of metals and common alloys.

● Peace: The learner avoids harming others when carrying out experiments to demonstrate the physical properties of metals.

Link to other subjects

●Pre-Technical Studies: Learner learns about common metals and alloys used in workshops.

● Agriculture and Nutrition: Learners use utensils made from metals and their alloys.
